def: A formal meeting, usually once a year, in which a manager and an employee discuss the employee's work over the past period and agree objectives for the next.

formal.ex: Each employee shall receive an [[annual performance appraisal]] conducted by his or her line manager.
formal.ex_us: Each employee shall receive an [[annual performance evaluation]] conducted by his or her manager.

everyday.ex: My [[appraisal]] is next Tuesday and I haven't filled in the form yet.
everyday.ex_us: My [[performance review]] is next Tuesday and I haven't filled out the form yet.

informal.ex: How did your [[annual review]] go?

collocations: to be due for an appraisal
note_fr: « Evaluation interview » est un calque. Britanniques : « appraisal » ; Américains : « performance review » ou « performance evaluation ». En France, l'entretien d'évaluation n'est pas imposé par la loi mais, s'il existe, le salarié doit avoir été informé au préalable des méthodes utilisées : précisez-le à un interlocuteur étranger.

def: A meeting required by French law in which employer and employee discuss the employee's career prospects and training needs, not his or her performance.

formal.ex: The [[statutory career development interview]] shall be held separately from the annual appraisal and recorded in writing.

everyday.ex: We're behind on our [[career development interviews]], and that's a compliance issue, not just a nice-to-have.

informal.ex: Think of it as a [[career conversation]] that happens to be compulsory.

collocations: to hold a career development interview
to keep a written record of the interview
to be offered an interview on returning from leave
note_fr: Ne le traduisez jamais par « appraisal » ni « professional interview » : cet entretien porte sur les perspectives d'évolution, pas sur l'évaluation du travail. Il n'a pas d'équivalent légal au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis. Sa périodicité et son intitulé ont été modifiés par le législateur (on parle désormais d'« entretien de parcours professionnel ») : vérifiez la règle en vigueur avant de donner un chiffre.

explain.written: The entretien professionnel is a meeting which French law requires employers to hold with each employee at regular intervals, devoted to career prospects and training needs rather than to the assessment of performance.
explain.spoken: It's a compulsory career conversation - nothing to do with the appraisal. You sit down with each employee every few years to talk about where they're heading and what training they need.

def: To decide, usually with the employee, what he or she is expected to achieve over a given period.

formal.ex: Objectives shall be [[set]] at the beginning of each financial year and notified to the employee in writing.

everyday.ex: We [[set objectives]] in January and review them in the summer.
everyday.ex_us: We [[set goals]] in January and review them in the summer.

note_fr: On dit « to set » (jamais « to fix ») des objectifs. « Objectives » domine au Royaume-Uni, « goals » aux États-Unis ; « targets » désigne plutôt des objectifs chiffrés. En droit français, des objectifs fixés unilatéralement doivent être réalistes et portés à la connaissance du salarié en début de période.

def: To achieve what one was asked to achieve in the period under review.

formal.ex: The employee has [[achieved]] all of the objectives set for the reference period.

everyday.ex: She [[met]] four of her five objectives, which is a good result in a difficult year.
everyday.ex_us: She [[met]] four of her five goals, which is a good result in a difficult year.

informal.ex: He's [[hit his targets]] three quarters running.
informal.ex_us: He's [[hit his numbers]] three quarters running.

collocations: to fall short of an objective
note_fr: Pas de « reach his objectives » dans ce contexte : on dit « meet », « achieve » ou, à l'oral, « hit ». Le contraire est « to miss a target » ou « to fall short of ».

def: Information given to someone about how well he or she is doing, so that he or she can improve or keep doing the right things.

formal.ex: Managers are expected to provide regular [[feedback]] on performance throughout the year.

everyday.ex: Could I get some [[feedback]] on the presentation before Friday?

informal.ex: Can you give me a [[steer]] on whether this is the right approach?
informal.ex_us: Can you give me some [[input]] on whether this is the right approach?

note_fr: « Feedback » est indénombrable : jamais « a feedback » ni « feedbacks ». Dites « some feedback », « a piece of feedback » ou « two points of feedback ». La préposition est « on » : « feedback on your report ».

def: To tell someone what you think of his or her work or behaviour, in order to help.

formal.ex: The appraiser shall [[provide feedback]] on each objective before an overall rating is proposed.

everyday.ex: I try to [[give feedback]] straight after the meeting, while it's still fresh.

informal.ex: I'll [[have a word with]] him about the way he handled that call.

collocations: to give someone feedback on something
to feed back to the team
note_fr: « To make a feedback » est un calque de « faire un retour ». Le verbe « to feed back » (en deux mots) existe surtout en anglais britannique : « I'll feed back to the team ». « To have a word with someone » annonce souvent une remarque un peu délicate.

def: What someone does well and what he or she needs to do better; the two standard headings of an appraisal.

formal.ex: The appraisal form records the employee's [[strengths and development needs]].

everyday.ex: Let's start with your [[strengths and areas for improvement]], and then look at next year.

informal.uk: what went well and what didn't
informal.us: what went well and what didn't
informal.ex: Just tell me [[what went well and what didn't]].

note_fr: N'écrivez pas « weak points » ni « axes of improvement » dans une évaluation : l'usage professionnel préfère « areas for improvement » ou « development areas ». « There's room for improvement » est une litote britannique qui peut signifier que le résultat est franchement insuffisant.

def: Organised activity through which employees learn the knowledge and skills they need for their work.

formal.ex: The company devotes a significant share of its payroll to [[vocational training]].

everyday.ex: We've got [[training]] on the new HR system all day Thursday.

note_fr: « Training » est indénombrable : « a training » et « trainings » sont à éviter à l'écrit soigné ; dites « a training course », « a training session ». Attention au faux ami : « formation » en anglais signifie création ou constitution (« the formation of a company »).

def: To take part in a course in order to learn something for one's work.

formal.ex: All newly appointed managers are required to [[undertake training]] in conducting appraisals.
formal.ex_us: All newly appointed managers are required to [[undergo training]] in conducting appraisals.

everyday.ex: I [[went on a course]] on employment law last month and it was excellent.
everyday.ex_us: I [[took a course]] on employment law last month and it was excellent.

collocations: to sign up for a course
to send someone on a course
note_fr: « To follow a training » est un calque. Les Britanniques disent « to go on a course » ou « to do a course », les Américains « to take a course » ou « to take a class ». « To send someone on a course » = envoyer quelqu'un en formation.

def: The abilities a person needs to do a job well, acquired through training or experience.

formal.ex: The role requires the [[skills and competencies]] described in the attached profile.

everyday.ex: She's got exactly the [[skills]] we need for the project.

informal.ex: We're losing a lot of [[know-how]] when he retires.

note_fr: « Competences » au sens de compétences professionnelles est rare et sonne français ; dites « skills », ou « competencies » dans un référentiel. « Competence » (singulier) désigne l'aptitude générale à faire son travail, et « competent » est un compliment plus tiède qu'en français.

def: The document in which a French employer sets out the training it has decided to provide for its employees over a given period.

formal.ex: The works council shall be consulted on the [[skills development plan]] for the coming year.

everyday.ex: The course isn't in this year's [[training plan]], but we may be able to find the budget.

collocations: to draw up the training plan
to include a course in the training plan
to consult the works council on the plan
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, un « training plan » est un simple outil de gestion, sans cadre légal. En France, le plan relève de l'initiative de l'employeur, les formations qui y figurent sont en principe suivies sur le temps de travail avec maintien de la rémunération, et le CSE est consulté : expliquez-le.

explain.written: The plan de développement des compétences is the document in which a French employer sets out the training it intends to provide at its own initiative; training under the plan is, as a rule, treated as working time and paid as such.
explain.spoken: It's the company's training plan - the courses the employer decides to put people on. In France it's a formal thing: it's generally done in working time, on full pay, and the works council is consulted.

def: An individual account, credited in euros, that every working person in France can use to pay for approved training of his or her own choice.

formal.ex: The Employee may use the rights accrued in his or her [[personal training account (CPF)]] to finance all or part of the course.

everyday.ex: She's paying for the course out of her [[personal training account]], so we only need to agree the dates.

informal.ex: You could always use your [[CPF]] for that.

collocations: to use one's personal training account
to top up an employee's account
note_fr: Aucun équivalent britannique ou américain : gardez le sigle et expliquez-le. Le compte appartient à la personne, la suit tout au long de sa carrière et s'utilise à son initiative ; l'accord de l'employeur n'est nécessaire que pour s'absenter pendant le temps de travail. Aux États-Unis, la notion la plus proche serait le « tuition assistance », qui reste un avantage facultatif de l'employeur.

explain.written: The compte personnel de formation (CPF) is an individual account, credited in euros and attached to the person rather than to the job, which may be used at the holder's initiative to pay for approved training.
explain.spoken: Everyone who works in France has a personal training account. Money goes into it each year, it follows you from job to job, and you decide what to spend it on.

def: To move someone to a more senior job, usually with more responsibility and higher pay.

formal.ex: With effect from 1 April, Ms Leroy is [[promoted]] to the position of Regional Sales Director.
formal.ex_us: Effective April 1, Ms. Leroy is [[promoted]] to the position of Regional Sales Director.

everyday.ex: He [[got promoted]] to team leader after only eighteen months.

informal.ex: She's ambitious and wants to [[move up]] quickly.

collocations: to put someone forward for promotion
a promotion to a senior role
note_fr: La préposition est « to » : « promoted to manager » (sans article devant la fonction), jamais « promoted as ». « To be up for promotion » = être candidat ou pressenti. « A promotion » désigne aussi une offre commerciale : le contexte tranche.

def: The movement of employees between jobs, departments or sites within the same organisation.

formal.ex: The Group encourages [[internal mobility]] and advertises all vacancies internally before recruiting externally.

everyday.ex: She's applied for an [[internal move]] to the Lyon office.
everyday.ex_us: She's applied for an [[internal transfer]] to the Lyon office.

collocations: to apply for an internal vacancy
to move across to another department
note_fr: « Mobility » seul évoque d'abord la mobilité géographique ou le handicap : précisez « internal mobility » ou, plus naturel à l'oral, « an internal move ». « To move across to » = passer dans un autre service au même niveau.

def: The way a person moves forward in working life, to more senior or more interesting jobs.

formal.ex: The agreement guarantees equal access to [[career progression]] for part-time employees.
formal.ex_us: The agreement guarantees equal access to [[career advancement]] for part-time employees.

everyday.ex: If you want to [[get on]] here, you need to be visible outside your own team.
everyday.ex_us: If you want to [[get ahead]] here, you need to be visible outside your own team.

note_fr: « Career evolution » est un calque : dites « career progression », « career development » ou « career advancement » (plus américain). « Prospects » rend très bien « perspectives d'évolution ».

def: The person an employee reports to directly and who is responsible for his or her work.

formal.ex: Requests for training must first be approved by the employee's [[line manager]].
formal.ex_us: Requests for training must first be approved by the employee's [[direct supervisor]].

everyday.ex: Have you talked to your [[line manager]] about it?
everyday.ex_us: Have you talked to your [[manager]] about it?

informal.ex: My [[boss]] is fine with it.

collocations: to raise something with one's line manager
note_fr: « N+1 » et « N+2 » ne sont pas compris hors de France : dites « line manager » (UK), « manager » ou « supervisor » (US), et « my manager's manager » ou « skip-level manager » (US) pour le N+2. « Hierarchical superior » est un calque pesant ; « responsible » n'est pas un nom en anglais.

def: An employee who reports directly to a given manager.

formal.ex: Each manager shall hold a mid-year review with every [[direct report]].

everyday.ex: She's got eight [[direct reports]], which is too many to coach properly.

informal.ex: I need to tell [[my team]] before it goes public.
informal.ex_us: I need to tell [[my people]] before it goes public.

collocations: to manage a team of ten
note_fr: « Collaborator » est un faux ami : en anglais il évoque la collaboration avec l'ennemi. Dites « direct report », « team member » ou « colleague ». « Subordinate » existe, mais il est jugé condescendant dans la plupart des entreprises.

def: A relationship in which a more experienced person regularly advises and supports a less experienced colleague.

formal.ex: All graduates joining the firm are enrolled in the [[mentoring programme]] for their first two years.
formal.ex_us: All graduates joining the firm are enrolled in the [[mentoring program]] for their first two years.

everyday.ex: She's offered to [[mentor]] two of the new team leaders.

informal.uk: to take someone under one's wing
informal.us: to take someone under one's wing
informal.ex: The finance director [[took him under her wing]] when he first arrived.

collocations: to act as a mentor to someone
to be paired with a mentor
note_fr: La personne accompagnée est le « mentee ». Le mentor conseille à partir de sa propre expérience, sans lien hiérarchique ; ne confondez pas avec le « coach » (voir cette entrée) ni avec le « tuteur » d'un alternant, qu'on rend plutôt par « workplace supervisor ».

def: Structured one-to-one support, often from a trained professional, that helps a person improve performance or develop a particular skill.

formal.ex: The package includes six sessions of [[executive coaching]] with an external provider.

everyday.ex: A good manager [[coaches]] people rather than telling them what to do.

collocations: to coach someone through a change
note_fr: « Accompaniment » est un faux ami (accompagnement musical ou garniture) : « accompagner un salarié » se dit « to support » ou « to coach ». Le coaching vise un objectif précis sur une durée limitée ; le mentoring est une relation plus longue et plus informelle.

def: An outside organisation that designs and delivers training courses for companies or individuals.

formal.ex: Courses shall be delivered by an [[external training provider]] selected by the Company.

everyday.ex: We've used the same [[training provider]] for years and the feedback is always good.
everyday.ex_us: We've used the same [[training vendor]] for years and the feedback is always good.

collocations: to commission a course from a provider
note_fr: « Training organism » est un calque : un « organism » est un être vivant. Un cours « delivered in-house » est assuré en interne. On dit « to deliver » ou « to run » a course, jamais « to animate ».

def: Training followed on a computer or phone, usually at the learner's own pace.

formal.ex: Employees are required to complete the [[online learning]] modules within thirty days of joining.

everyday.ex: It's a forty-minute [[e-learning]] module; you can do it whenever suits you.

informal.ex: I did an [[online course]] on Excel over the weekend.

note_fr: « Distance learning » désigne plutôt un cursus long suivi à distance. « Self-paced » = à son rythme, en autonomie ; « live online » ou « virtual classroom » = classe virtuelle avec formateur. On dit « to complete a module », pas « to realise ».

def: The skills or knowledge that employees lack and that training could provide.

formal.ex: Managers shall identify the [[training requirements]] of their teams during the annual appraisal round.

everyday.ex: Let's go through your [[training needs]] for next year before we finish.

note_fr: « Needs in training » est un calque : l'anglais empile les noms (« training needs »). « Recueil des besoins » se dit « collecting training requests » ou « gathering training needs », pas « collect of needs ».

def: An organisation's ability to keep its employees, and the measures it takes to do so.

formal.ex: The report recommends a series of measures designed to improve [[employee retention]] among junior staff.

everyday.ex: We're good at hiring; we're less good at [[holding on to people]].

note_fr: « Fidelisation » et « loyalisation » n'existent pas en anglais des RH : on parle de « retention » et du verbe « to retain ». « Loyalty » désigne le sentiment de fidélité, pas la politique.

def: The rate at which employees leave an organisation and are replaced.

formal.ex: [[Labour turnover]] in the division rose sharply over the last financial year.
formal.ex_us: [[Employee turnover]] in the division rose sharply over the last fiscal year.

everyday.ex: [[Staff turnover]] is high in the call centre, and exit interviews tell us why.
everyday.ex_us: [[Turnover]] is high in the call center, and exit interviews tell us why.

informal.ex: There's been a lot of [[churn]] in that team.

note_fr: Double piège : en anglais britannique, « turnover » seul désigne d'abord le chiffre d'affaires. Précisez « staff turnover ». « Attrition » désigne les départs naturels non remplacés ou, plus largement, le taux de départ.

def: The degree to which employees feel committed to their work and their organisation and are willing to put effort into it.

formal.ex: [[Employee engagement]] is measured annually by means of an anonymous survey.

everyday.ex: The team's far more [[engaged]] since the reorganisation.
everyday.ex_us: The team's far more [[engaged]] since the reorganization.

informal.ex: [[Morale]] has really picked up since she took over.

note_fr: Faux ami partiel : « engagement » seul signifie d'abord fiançailles ou rendez-vous. Pour « s'engager à faire quelque chose », dites « to commit to » ou « to undertake to », pas « to engage oneself ».

def: A questionnaire sent to all employees to find out how they feel about their work, their managers and the organisation.

formal.ex: The results of the [[employee engagement survey]] will be presented to the works council in aggregate form only.

everyday.ex: The [[staff survey]] closes on Friday and we're only at fifty per cent.
everyday.ex_us: The [[employee survey]] closes on Friday and we're only at fifty percent.

collocations: to act on the survey results
note_fr: On dit « to run » ou « to carry out » a survey, et non « to make » ; « to fill in » (UK) ou « to fill out » (US) a survey. « Enquête » ne se traduit par « inquiry » ou « investigation » que lorsqu'il s'agit d'établir des faits.

def: Teaching employees new or more advanced skills so that they can do their present job better or take on a bigger one.

formal.ex: The agreement provides for the [[upskilling]] of all production staff affected by the new equipment.

everyday.ex: We'd rather [[upskill]] the people we have than hire from outside.

informal.ex: Give her a month to [[get up to speed]] on the new tool.

collocations: to bring someone up to speed
note_fr: « To rise in competences » ne veut rien dire en anglais. « To upskill » est transitif (« to upskill the team ») ou intransitif. « To get up to speed » concerne une prise en main rapide plutôt qu'un vrai développement des compétences.

def: Learning the skills needed for a different job or occupation.

formal.ex: Employees whose roles are at risk will be offered [[reskilling]] for positions in the new logistics centre.
formal.ex_us: Employees whose roles are at risk will be offered [[reskilling]] for positions in the new logistics center.

everyday.ex: He [[retrained]] as a data analyst after ten years in sales.

informal.ex: She's thinking about a complete [[career change]].

note_fr: « Reconversion » est un faux ami : en anglais, le mot ne s'emploie pas pour les personnes (on l'entend pour un bâtiment ou un site industriel, et encore). Dites « retraining », « reskilling » ou « a career change ». Construction : « to retrain as » + métier.

def: The part of the appraisal in which employees judge their own performance before meeting their manager.

formal.ex: The employee shall complete the [[self-assessment]] section of the form at least one week before the meeting.
formal.ex_us: The employee shall complete the [[self-evaluation]] section of the form at least one week before the meeting.

everyday.ex: I always find the [[self-assessment]] the hardest part to write.
everyday.ex_us: I always find the [[self-review]] the hardest part to write.

note_fr: « Auto-evaluation » n'est pas idiomatique : le préfixe anglais est « self- ». Au Royaume-Uni, « self-assessment » désigne aussi la déclaration de revenus : le contexte suffit en général à lever l'ambiguïté.

def: The overall grade or label given to an employee's performance at the end of the appraisal.

formal.ex: The [[overall performance rating]] is proposed by the line manager and confirmed after calibration.
formal.ex_us: The [[overall performance rating]] is proposed by the manager and confirmed after calibration.

everyday.ex: He wasn't happy with his [[rating]] and has asked to see me.

note_fr: « Note » ou « notation » ne se traduisent pas ici par « note » ni « mark » (scolaire) : on parle de « rating ». « Appreciation » signifie gratitude ou hausse de valeur, jamais appréciation portée sur le travail.

def: To perform better than the level required for the job; a common label on rating scales.

formal.ex: An employee whose performance consistently [[exceeds expectations]] may be considered for accelerated progression.

everyday.ex: She's [[done better than expected]] on every one of her objectives.

informal.ex: He really [[went above and beyond]] on the migration project.

note_fr: On dit « to exceed » ou « to surpass » expectations, jamais « to overpass ». L'échelle classique : « below expectations », « meets expectations », « exceeds expectations », « outstanding ».

def: A regular private meeting between a manager and one member of the team.

formal.ex: Managers are expected to hold a [[one-to-one meeting]] with each team member at least once a month.
formal.ex_us: Managers are expected to hold a [[one-on-one meeting]] with each team member at least once a month.

everyday.ex: Can we cover that in our [[one-to-one]] on Thursday?
everyday.ex_us: Can we cover that in our [[one-on-one]] on Thursday?

informal.ex: Let's have a quick [[catch-up]] tomorrow morning.
informal.ex_us: Let's have a quick [[check-in]] tomorrow morning.

collocations: to put a one-to-one in the diary
note_fr: Vraie différence de variété : « one-to-one » au Royaume-Uni, « one-on-one » aux États-Unis. « A point » ne veut pas dire réunion : « faire un point » se dit « to have a catch-up » ou « to touch base ». « Diary » (UK) = « calendar » (US).

def: A short document agreed between employee and manager listing the skills the employee wants to develop and how he or she will do it.

formal.ex: A [[personal development plan]] shall be agreed at the end of each appraisal and reviewed at mid-year.
formal.ex_us: An [[individual development plan]] shall be agreed at the end of each performance review and reviewed at midyear.

everyday.ex: Let's put that in your [[development plan]] so it doesn't get forgotten.

informal.ex: Have you updated your [[PDP]] yet?

collocations: to review the plan at mid-year
note_fr: Les sigles diffèrent : « PDP » au Royaume-Uni, « IDP » aux États-Unis. Ne confondez pas avec le « PIP » (performance improvement plan), qui est un plan de redressement en cas d'insuffisance et n'a rien d'un outil de développement.

def: Everything an organisation does to attract, identify, develop and keep the people it most needs.

formal.ex: Responsibility for [[talent management]] lies with the Group HR Director.

everyday.ex: She runs [[talent management]] for the whole of Europe.

note_fr: « Talent » est le plus souvent indénombrable (« to attract talent ») ; « talents » au pluriel pour désigner des personnes sonne français, même si l'on dit « a talent » pour un don. Ne traduisez pas « gestion » par « gestion » : c'est toujours « management ».

def: The series of jobs a person holds, or could hold, over working life within a profession or an organisation.

formal.ex: The framework defines a clear [[career pathway]] from technician to senior engineer.
formal.ex_us: The framework defines a clear [[career path]] from technician to senior engineer.

everyday.ex: There's no obvious [[career path]] for specialists here, and that's why they leave.

informal.ex: What do you see as your [[next step]]?

collocations: to map out a career path
to follow an unusual career path
note_fr: « Professional course » ou « professional path » sont des calques. Pour le parcours déjà accompli, on dit plutôt « career history », « background » ou « track record » : « tell me about your background ».

fr: formation sur le tas / en situation de travail
def: Training given at the workplace while the employee is actually doing the job.

formal.ex: [[On-the-job training]] is provided by an experienced colleague during the first three months.

everyday.ex: Most of what I know about payroll I [[learnt on the job]].
everyday.ex_us: Most of what I know about payroll I [[learned on the job]].

informal.ex: It took me a good six months to [[learn the ropes]].

collocations: to train someone on the job
to pick something up as you go
note_fr: L'expression n'a rien de péjoratif en anglais, contrairement à « sur le tas ». « Hands-on » = pratique, concret. Orthographe : « learnt » (UK) ou « learned » (US).

def: A person who teaches skills to employees.

formal.ex: Each session is led by a certified [[trainer]] with experience of the sector.
formal.ex_us: Each session is led by a certified [[instructor]] with experience in the sector.

everyday.ex: The [[trainer]] was brilliant; she kept twelve managers awake for a whole afternoon.

note_fr: « Formator » n'existe pas, et « animator » désigne un dessinateur de dessins animés : celui qui anime un atelier est un « facilitator », et il le « runs » ou le « facilitates ». « Trainers » désigne aussi des baskets en anglais britannique.

def: In France, a structured review of a person's skills, aptitudes and motivations, carried out with an outside adviser in order to define a career or training plan.

formal.ex: The Company agrees to bear the cost of a [[skills assessment (bilan de compétences)]] carried out by a provider of the Employee's choice.

everyday.ex: She's doing a [[skills assessment]] to work out what she wants to do next.
everyday.ex_us: She's doing a [[career assessment]] to figure out what she wants to do next.

collocations: to carry out a skills assessment
the findings belong to the employee
note_fr: « Competence balance » ne veut rien dire. Il n'existe pas de dispositif légal équivalent au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis, où l'on parlerait de « career counselling » (US : « career counseling »). Point essentiel à expliquer : les conclusions appartiennent au salarié et ne peuvent être communiquées à l'employeur qu'avec son accord.

explain.written: The bilan de compétences is a structured assessment of an individual's skills, aptitudes and motivations, carried out by an external provider with a view to defining a career or training plan; its findings belong to the individual and may be passed on to the employer only with his or her consent.
explain.spoken: It's a sort of in-depth career review with an outside adviser. You look at your skills and what motivates you and come out with a plan - and the results are yours; your employer only sees them if you agree.

def: A French procedure by which a person obtains all or part of a recognised qualification on the strength of experience, without following the usual course.

formal.ex: Employees may obtain the qualification through [[validation of prior experience (VAE)]], subject to assessment by a panel.

everyday.us: to get credit for one's experience
everyday.ex: He never went to university, so he's [[getting his experience accredited]] to obtain the degree.
everyday.ex_us: He never went to college, so he's [[getting credit for his experience]] to earn the degree.

collocations: to apply for validation of prior experience
to be assessed by a panel
to obtain part of a qualification
note_fr: Les notions voisines sont « recognition of prior learning » (RPL) au Royaume-Uni et « prior learning assessment » ou « credit for prior learning » aux États-Unis, mais elles donnent le plus souvent des dispenses ou des crédits, rarement le diplôme entier. « Acquis » ne se traduit pas par « acquired » employé comme nom.

explain.written: Validation des acquis de l'expérience (VAE) is a procedure under French law by which a person may be awarded all or part of a recognised qualification on the basis of his or her experience, after assessment by a panel.
explain.spoken: It's a way of turning experience into a qualification. You put together a file showing what you've actually done, a panel assesses it, and you can come out with the full diploma without going back to school.

def: A system combining periods of paid work in a company with periods of study at a training centre, leading to a qualification.

formal.ex: The Company undertakes to recruit a set number of young people on [[work-study contracts]] each year.

everyday.ex: We've got two [[work-study students]] in the team; they're with us three weeks out of four.

informal.ex: Our [[alternant]] is back at school next week.

collocations: to be on a work-study contract
to split one's time between school and the company
note_fr: « Alternance » et « alternation » ne sont pas compris. En France, l'alternance recouvre deux contrats de travail (apprentissage et professionnalisation). Au Royaume-Uni, on parlera d'« apprenticeship » ; aux États-Unis, « work-study » évoque surtout des emplois étudiants aidés, et « co-op program » ou « apprenticeship » sont plus proches. Le tuteur ou maître d'apprentissage est un « workplace supervisor » ou « workplace mentor ».

explain.written: Alternance is the French system of work-study training, under which a person is employed by a company on a specific type of employment contract while studying for a qualification at a training centre.
explain.spoken: It's work-study: the person is a proper employee, on a contract, and spends part of the time with us and part at school, working towards a qualification.

def: Training that employees must complete because the law, a regulator or company policy requires it.

formal.ex: Failure to complete [[mandatory training]] within the prescribed time may be recorded in the employee's file.

everyday.ex: Everyone's got [[compliance training]] to finish by the end of the month.

informal.ex: People see it as a [[box-ticking exercise]], which is a pity.
informal.ex_us: People see it as a [[check-the-box exercise]], which is a pity.

collocations: to be overdue on a module
note_fr: « Obligatory » est possible mais rare ; « mandatory » et « compulsory » sont les mots usuels. « Statutory training » désigne spécifiquement ce qu'impose la loi. « To tick a box » (UK) = « to check a box » (US).

def: The HR function responsible for training employees and developing their skills.

formal.ex: The Head of [[Learning and Development]] reports annually on the implementation of the training plan.

everyday.ex: Ask [[L&D]]; they'll know whether there's a course on that.

note_fr: Le « service formation » est aujourd'hui « L&D » (prononcé « L and D ») ou « Learning » ; « training department » date un peu. « Learner » est le terme courant pour le stagiaire de formation ; « trainee » désigne plutôt un débutant en poste, et « stagiaire » au sens français se dit « intern ».

def: Training delivered by a trainer to a group of people who are physically in the same room.

formal.ex: The programme comprises two days of [[face-to-face training]] followed by three online modules.
formal.ex_us: The program comprises two days of [[instructor-led training]] followed by three online modules.

everyday.ex: People still prefer [[classroom training]] for the management courses.

informal.ex: Is it online or [[in person]]?

note_fr: « Presential » n'existe pas en anglais : dites « face-to-face », « in person », « classroom » ou « on-site ». « Distanciel » se rend par « remote », « online » ou « virtual ».

def: A way of training that combines face-to-face sessions with online learning.

formal.ex: The leadership curriculum is delivered through [[blended learning]] over a period of six months.

everyday.uk: a mix of online and face-to-face
everyday.us: a mix of online and in-person
everyday.ex: It's [[a mix of online and face-to-face]], so people are only out of the office for two days.
everyday.ex_us: It's [[a mix of online and in-person]], so people are only out of the office for two days.

collocations: to combine online modules with workshops
note_fr: « Mixed training » se comprend mais ne se dit pas. « Hybrid » qualifie plutôt une séance suivie en même temps sur place et à distance. « Learning journey » est le jargon courant pour « parcours de formation ».

def: A systematic study of the gap between the skills employees have and the skills the organisation needs, used to decide what training to provide.

formal.ex: A [[training needs analysis]] shall be conducted before the plan is drawn up.
formal.ex_us: A [[training needs assessment]] shall be conducted before the plan is drawn up.

everyday.ex: We haven't done a proper [[TNA]] for three years, and it shows.
everyday.ex_us: We haven't done a proper [[needs assessment]] in three years, and it shows.

collocations: to carry out a training needs analysis
note_fr: Le sigle « TNA » est britannique ; les Américains disent plutôt « needs assessment ». Pluriel irrégulier : « one analysis, two analyses » (/əˈnæləsiːz/).

fr: formation de recyclage / remise à niveau
def: A short course that brings existing knowledge or skills up to date.

formal.ex: Certified first-aiders shall attend [[refresher training]] at the intervals laid down by the regulations.

everyday.ex: I could do with a [[refresher course]] on the appraisal system before the next round.
everyday.ex_us: I could use a [[refresher course]] on the review system before the next cycle.

informal.ex: I need to [[brush up on]] my employment law.

collocations: to keep one's skills up to date
note_fr: « Recycling » ne s'applique qu'aux déchets : pour les personnes, dites « refresher » ou « update ». « I could do with » (UK) = « I could use » (US) = j'aurais bien besoin de.

def: An official record showing that a person has completed a course of study or training or passed an examination.

formal.ex: The course leads to a [[recognised qualification]] listed in the national register.
formal.ex_us: The course leads to a [[recognized credential]] listed in the national register.

everyday.ex: She's studying for an HR [[qualification]] in the evenings.
everyday.ex_us: She's studying for an HR [[certification]] in the evenings.

collocations: to hold a degree in law
a course leading to a qualification
note_fr: « Diploma » est un faux ami partiel : il désigne un type précis de titre, souvent inférieur au « degree » universitaire (au Royaume-Uni), ou le diplôme de fin d'études secondaires (aux États-Unis). Pour « diplômé de », dites « she has a degree in » ou « she graduated from ». « Formation certifiante » = « a course leading to a qualification ».

def: The learning that people undertake throughout their careers to keep their knowledge and skills up to date.

formal.ex: Members are required to record at least the prescribed number of hours of [[continuing professional development]] each year.
formal.ex_us: Members are required to record at least the prescribed number of hours of [[continuing education]] each year.

everyday.ex: The conference counts towards my [[CPD]].
everyday.ex_us: The conference counts toward my [[professional development]].

note_fr: « Continuous formation » est un double calque. « CPD » est un sigle britannique lié aux professions réglementées ; aux États-Unis, on parle de « continuing education » (CE). La « formation professionnelle tout au long de la vie » se dit « lifelong learning ».

def: A meeting held halfway through the year to check progress against objectives and adjust them if necessary.

formal.ex: Objectives may be revised at the [[mid-year review]] where business circumstances have changed.
formal.ex_us: Objectives may be revised at the [[midyear review]] where business circumstances have changed.

everyday.ex: We've got [[mid-year check-ins]] coming up, so have a think about where you are.
everyday.ex_us: We've got [[midyear check-ins]] coming up, so think about where you are.

note_fr: « Faire le point » se dit « to take stock » ou « to review progress », pas « to make the point » (qui signifie faire valoir un argument). « Have a think » est typiquement britannique.

def: A goal-setting method in which each ambitious objective is paired with a few measurable results that show whether it has been achieved.

formal.ex: The division sets its [[objectives and key results]] quarterly and publishes them internally.

everyday.ex: Our [[OKRs]] for this quarter are far too vague; nobody can tell whether we've met them.

note_fr: Le sigle se prononce lettre à lettre et prend un s au pluriel. Les OKR sont en principe un outil de pilotage, souvent dissocié de la rémunération. Pour un objectif individuel classique, on parle d'objectif « SMART » (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound).

def: A figure used to measure how well a person, a team or an organisation is doing against its objectives.

formal.ex: Progress shall be measured against the [[key performance indicators]] set out in the schedule.

everyday.ex: Time to fill isn't a great [[KPI]] for a recruitment team on its own.

informal.ex: Which [[metrics]] are we actually tracking?

note_fr: On mesure « against » des indicateurs : « performance against KPIs ». « Indicator » seul est rare à l'oral, où l'on dit « KPI », « metric » ou « measure ». « To follow an indicator » est un calque : dites « to track » ou « to monitor ».

def: A deliberately demanding objective that goes beyond what the person is confident of achieving.

formal.ex: In addition to the core objectives, one [[stretch objective]] may be agreed with the employee.
formal.ex_us: In addition to the core goals, one [[stretch goal]] may be agreed upon with the employee.

everyday.ex: Ten per cent is the target; fifteen is the [[stretch goal]].
everyday.ex_us: Ten percent is the target; fifteen is the [[stretch goal]].

informal.ex: Doubling the numbers in a year is [[a big ask]].

note_fr: « Ambitious » convient mais « stretch » est le terme consacré. « Challenging » est positif en anglais (stimulant, exigeant). Attention : en droit français, un objectif irréaliste ne peut pas être opposé au salarié ; un « stretch goal » doit donc rester atteignable.

fr: être en bonne voie (d'atteindre un objectif)
def: To be making the progress needed to achieve an objective by the agreed date.

formal.ex: At the mid-year stage, three of the four objectives [[are progressing satisfactorily]].
formal.ex_us: At the midyear stage, three of the four objectives [[are progressing satisfactorily]].

everyday.ex: You're [[on track]] to meet all four objectives, which is very good going.

informal.ex: It's slow, but we're [[getting there]].

collocations: to be on track to meet an objective
note_fr: On dit « on track to meet » ou « on track for » : « on track for promotion ». Les contraires usuels : « behind », « off track », « slipping ». « On the good way » est un calque.

def: Comments on what someone could do better, given in a specific and helpful way so that the person can act on them.

formal.ex: Appraisers are trained to give [[constructive feedback]] based on specific, observed examples.

everyday.ex: I've got some [[constructive feedback]] on the workshop, if you're open to it.

informal.ex: Can I give you [[a few pointers]] for next time?

collocations: to focus on behaviour, not personality
note_fr: Ne dites pas « a critic » (c'est une personne) ni « to critic » : le nom est « criticism », le verbe « to criticise » (US : « criticize »), et tous deux sont nettement négatifs. « Constructive feedback » est l'euphémisme professionnel pour une remarque critique.

fr: accueillir / prendre en compte un retour
def: To listen to comments about one's work and actually change something as a result.

formal.ex: The employee has demonstrably [[acted on the feedback]] received at the previous review.

everyday.ex: She [[took the feedback on board]] and her last two reports were much tighter.
everyday.ex_us: She [[took the feedback to heart]] and her last two reports were much tighter.

informal.uk: to take it on the chin
informal.ex: It was a tough message, but he [[took it on the chin]].
informal.ex_us: It was a tough message, but he [[took it in stride]].

note_fr: « To take on board » est surtout britannique ; un Américain dira plutôt « to take it to heart » ou « to incorporate the feedback ». « To get defensive » = se braquer ; « don't take it personally » = n'y voyez rien de personnel.

def: The set of grades or labels, from lowest to highest, used to rate performance.

formal.ex: Performance is assessed on a five-point [[rating scale]] ranging from 'unsatisfactory' to 'outstanding'.

everyday.ex: We moved from a five-point to a four-point [[scale]] so that managers couldn't sit in the middle.

collocations: to rate someone on a scale of one to five
to sit in the middle of the scale
note_fr: On note « on a scale of one to five » ou « on a five-point scale » ; « from one to five » se dit aussi, mais « a scale from five » non. « Central tendency » désigne la tendance des managers à noter tout le monde au milieu.

def: The process of identifying and preparing people who could take over key roles when the present holders leave.

formal.ex: [[Succession planning]] for members of the executive committee is reviewed annually by the board.

everyday.ex: We've no [[succession plan]] for the plant manager, and he retires in two years.
everyday.ex_us: We have no [[succession plan]] for the plant manager, and he retires in two years.

informal.ex: They've [[lined her up]] to take over from him.

collocations: to groom someone for a role
note_fr: « Succession » évoque aussi l'héritage, mais « succession planning » est sans ambiguïté en entreprise. On « takes over from » son prédécesseur ; « to succeed someone » existe mais reste plus soutenu. Les étiquettes usuelles : « ready now », « ready in one to two years ».

def: An employee judged capable of rising quickly to much more senior roles.

formal.ex: [[High-potential employees]] are identified through the annual talent review and offered a dedicated development programme.
formal.ex_us: [[High-potential employees]] are identified through the annual talent review and offered a dedicated development program.

everyday.ex: She's one of our [[high potentials]]; we need to give her something bigger soon.

informal.ex: He's on the [[HiPo]] list.

collocations: to have the potential to go further
note_fr: Ne confondez pas « high potential » (capacité à évoluer) et « high performer » (excellents résultats dans le poste actuel) : toute la revue des talents repose sur cette distinction. « High potential » s'emploie comme nom ou comme adjectif (avec trait d'union).

def: The group of employees identified as able to fill more senior or key roles in the future.

formal.ex: The [[talent pool]] for senior management roles remains insufficiently diverse.

everyday.ex: Our [[talent pipeline]] for plant managers is looking thin.

collocations: to draw on the talent pool
note_fr: « Pool » = le réservoir à un instant donné ; « pipeline » insiste sur le flux de personnes en préparation. « Vivier » ne se traduit ni par « fishpond » ni par « nursery ».

def: A document describing the skills and behaviours expected in each role or at each level of an organisation.

formal.ex: Employees are assessed against the behaviours described in the [[competency framework]].
formal.ex_us: Employees are assessed against the behaviors described in the [[competency model]].

everyday.ex: The [[competency framework]] hasn't been updated since before anyone worked remotely.
everyday.ex_us: The [[competency model]] hasn't been updated since before anyone worked remotely.

collocations: to assess someone against a framework
note_fr: « Referential » est un adjectif en anglais, jamais un nom : « a referential of competences » est incompréhensible. Dites « framework » (UK) ou « model » (US). Dans ce contexte, le pluriel usuel est « competencies ».

def: Personal and social abilities, such as communicating, listening and working with others, as opposed to technical knowledge.

formal.ex: The role calls for strong [[interpersonal skills]] and the ability to influence without authority.

everyday.ex: Technically he's excellent; it's the [[soft skills]] he needs to work on.

informal.ex: She's got great [[people skills]].

collocations: to work on one's soft skills
note_fr: « Savoir-être » n'a pas de traduction littérale : dites « soft skills », « interpersonal skills » ou « behaviours ». « Savoir-faire » se rend par « know-how » ou « expertise », et les compétences techniques par « hard skills » ou « technical skills ».

def: Skills acquired in one job or sector that can be used in another.

formal.ex: The assessment identifies the [[transferable skills]] on which a move to another occupation could be based.

everyday.ex: You've got more [[transferable skills]] than you think; project management is the same everywhere.

collocations: to carry skills over to a new role
note_fr: Accent tonique sur la deuxième syllabe : transFERable. « Transversal skills » se rencontre dans les textes européens mais reste rare chez les anglophones, qui disent « transferable » ou « cross-functional ».

def: The difference between the skills an organisation or a person has and the skills that are needed.

formal.ex: The analysis reveals a significant [[skills gap]] in data analysis across the finance function.

everyday.ex: There's a real [[gap]] on the digital side that we need to close before next year.

note_fr: On « closes », « bridges » ou « addresses » a gap ; « to fill a gap » se dit surtout d'un poste ou d'un manque ponctuel. « Skills shortage » désigne une pénurie sur le marché du travail, « skills gap » un écart en interne.

def: A group of jobs that involve similar work and require similar skills, at different levels of seniority.

formal.ex: Each position is assigned to a [[job family]] and to a level within that family.

everyday.ex: Moving from one [[job family]] to another is possible, but nobody explains how.

collocations: to belong to a job family
note_fr: « Métier » n'a pas d'équivalent unique : « job », « occupation », « profession », « trade » (métier manuel) ou « function » selon le cas. « Filière » se rend par « job family », « track » ou « stream ».

def: A change to a different job at the same level of seniority and pay, usually to gain new experience.

formal.ex: A [[lateral transfer]] does not in itself give rise to any change in grade or remuneration.

everyday.ex: It's a [[sideways move]], but it gets her the operational experience she's missing.
everyday.ex_us: It's a [[lateral move]], but it gets her the operational experience she's missing.

note_fr: « Horizontal mobility » appartient au vocabulaire des sociologues. « Sideways move » peut être légèrement péjoratif (mise sur une voie de garage) : insistez sur l'intérêt du poste si vous l'employez.

fr: ne pas obtenir une promotion attendue

term.uk: to be passed over for promotion
term.us: to be passed over for promotion

def: Not to be given a promotion that one expected or deserved, when someone else is chosen instead.

formal.uk: to be unsuccessful in one's application for promotion
formal.us: to be unsuccessful in one's application for promotion
formal.ex: Employees who [[are unsuccessful in their application for promotion]] are entitled to feedback on request.

everyday.uk: to be passed over for promotion
everyday.us: to be passed over for promotion
everyday.ex: He's been [[passed over for promotion]] twice and he's starting to look elsewhere.

informal.ex: She [[missed out]] to an external candidate.

collocations: to be overlooked for a role
to miss out on a promotion
note_fr: L'expression suggère une injustice ressentie : n'écrivez pas « passed over » dans un document officiel, où « unsuccessful » est le terme neutre. « To miss out on » = passer à côté de.

def: A route by which selected employees are promoted more quickly than usual.

formal.ex: Graduates selected for the [[accelerated development programme]] rotate through three functions in two years.
formal.ex_us: Graduates selected for the [[accelerated development program]] rotate through three functions in two years.

everyday.ex: They've [[fast-tracked]] her into a regional role.

informal.ex: He's very much [[on the fast track]].

note_fr: Nom en deux mots (« the fast track »), verbe et adjectif avec trait d'union (« to fast-track », « a fast-track scheme »). « Scheme » est neutre en anglais britannique (dispositif) mais péjoratif en américain (combine) : dites « program » aux États-Unis.

fr: observation en situation de travail (« vis ma vie »)
def: Spending time following a colleague at work in order to learn what the job involves.

formal.ex: The induction includes two days of [[job shadowing]] in the customer service team.
formal.ex_us: The orientation includes two days of [[job shadowing]] on the customer service team.

everyday.ex: Why don't you [[shadow]] Priya for a week and see whether the role appeals?

informal.ex: I [[sat in with]] the payroll team for a day.

collocations: to sit in on a meeting
to see the job at first hand
note_fr: « To shadow » est transitif : « to shadow someone ». « To sit in on a meeting » = assister à une réunion en observateur. « In the team » (UK) devient « on the team » (US).

def: Training and experience designed to prepare people to lead teams and organisations.

formal.ex: Participation in the [[leadership development programme]] is by nomination only.
formal.ex_us: Participation in the [[leadership development program]] is by nomination only.

everyday.ex: She's been put on the [[leadership programme]] this year.
everyday.ex_us: She's been put in the [[leadership program]] this year.

collocations: to nominate someone for a programme
note_fr: « Leadership » désigne aussi, collectivement, l'équipe dirigeante : « senior leadership has approved it ». « Cadres dirigeants » se rend par « senior leaders » ou « senior executives » ; « cadre » au sens français n'a pas d'équivalent et ne se traduit pas par « executive » pour un cadre ordinaire.

def: What an employee hopes to do or become in his or her working life.

formal.ex: The interview provides an opportunity for the employee to set out his or her [[career aspirations]].

everyday.ex: Tell me a bit about [[where you want to go]] over the next few years.

collocations: to see oneself in a role
to be keen to move into management
note_fr: « Wishes of evolution » est un calque. Question naturelle en entretien : « Where do you see yourself in three years' time? ». « To manage expectations » = éviter de laisser espérer ce qu'on ne pourra pas offrir.

def: A conversation with an employee who is leaving, held to understand the reasons for the departure and improve retention.

formal.ex: All employees who resign shall be offered an [[exit interview]] with a member of the HR department.

everyday.ex: Her [[exit interview]] was eye-opening; it wasn't about pay at all.

note_fr: Rien de légal ni d'obligatoire : c'est un outil de fidélisation, à ne pas confondre avec l'entretien préalable à un licenciement. « A leaver » (UK) = un salarié sur le départ. Le « stay interview » est son pendant préventif : on demande aux salariés en poste ce qui les ferait rester.

def: Everything an employee encounters and feels in dealing with the organisation, from the first day to the last.

formal.ex: The strategy places [[employee experience]] on the same footing as customer experience.

everyday.uk: what it's like to work here
everyday.us: what it's like to work here
everyday.ex: The survey is really about [[what it's like to work here]].

note_fr: Ne dites pas « collaborator experience ». Rappel : « experience » signifie à la fois vécu et ancienneté professionnelle, mais jamais expérience scientifique (« experiment »).

def: Showing employees, by words or rewards, that their work and achievements are noticed and valued.

formal.ex: The scheme provides for the [[recognition]] of exceptional contributions outside the annual review cycle.
formal.ex_us: The program provides for the [[recognition]] of exceptional contributions outside the annual review cycle.

everyday.ex: You should [[give her credit]] for that in front of the team.

informal.ex: Everyone likes [[a pat on the back]] now and then.

collocations: to take the credit for something
note_fr: « Reconnaissant » se dit « grateful », pas « recognising ». « To acknowledge » convient pour saluer un effort : « I'd like to acknowledge the work the team has done ». « To feel valued » rend bien « se sentir reconnu ».

def: A very short survey sent frequently to employees to track how their mood or opinion is changing.

formal.ex: A quarterly [[pulse survey]] supplements the annual engagement survey.

everyday.ex: We ran a [[pulse survey]] after the announcement and the mood was better than we feared.

informal.ex: Let's do a quick [[temperature check]] with the team.

collocations: to take the pulse of the organisation
note_fr: L'image est médicale : « to take the pulse of » = prendre le pouls. « Barometer » existe mais s'emploie peu pour une enquête interne. « Survey fatigue » = lassitude face aux sondages à répétition.

fr: assurer l'intérim d'un poste supérieur (faisant fonction)

term.us: to serve in an acting capacity

def: To do a more senior job temporarily, for example while the usual holder is absent or the post is vacant.

formal.uk: to be appointed on an acting basis
formal.us: to be appointed on an acting basis
formal.ex: Ms Ahmed is [[appointed on an acting basis]] to the post of Finance Director pending recruitment.
formal.ex_us: Ms. Ahmed is [[appointed on an acting basis]] to the position of Finance Director pending recruitment.

everyday.ex: He's been [[acting up]] as head of department since March.
everyday.ex_us: He's been [[filling in as interim]] head of department since March.

informal.ex: She's [[holding the fort]] until the new director arrives.
informal.ex_us: She's [[holding down the fort]] until the new director arrives.

collocations: to step up into a role
note_fr: Attention : « to act up » au sens d'assurer un intérim est strictement britannique ; partout ailleurs, et aussi au Royaume-Uni, il signifie se tenir mal ou tomber en panne. Avec un Américain, dites « acting manager » ou « interim manager ». « Interim » ne veut jamais dire travail temporaire (« agency work »).

fr: gestion des emplois et des parcours professionnels (GEPP)
def: Forward planning of the jobs and skills an organisation will need, and of the measures (training, mobility, recruitment) required to get there.

formal.uk: forward planning of jobs and career paths (GEPP)
formal.us: forward planning of jobs and career paths (GEPP)
formal.ex: Management and the representative unions shall open negotiations on the [[forward planning of jobs and career paths (GEPP)]].

everyday.ex: What the French call GEPP is essentially [[strategic workforce planning]], except that you have to negotiate it with the unions.

collocations: jobs at risk and emerging jobs
note_fr: Le sigle (anciennement GPEC) n'est connu qu'en France. L'outil de gestion équivalent s'appelle « strategic workforce planning » ; la différence est juridique : en France, les entreprises d'une certaine taille doivent négocier périodiquement sur ce thème avec les organisations syndicales, ce qui n'existe ni au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis.

explain.written: GEPP (gestion des emplois et des parcours professionnels) is the forward planning of jobs, skills and career paths, a subject on which larger French companies are required to negotiate periodically with their trade unions.
explain.spoken: GEPP is the French version of strategic workforce planning. The twist is that, above a certain size, you have to sit down with the unions and negotiate it.

fr: état des lieux récapitulatif du parcours professionnel
def: In France, a written review, carried out at longer intervals fixed by law, checking that the employee has had the required career interviews and at least some training or progression.

formal.uk: periodic review of the employee's career path
formal.us: periodic review of the employee's career path
formal.ex: The [[periodic review of the employee's career path]] shall be recorded in a document, a copy of which is given to the employee.

everyday.ex: The [[stocktake]] is where you check that the interviews actually happened and that the person has had some training.
everyday.ex_us: The [[career review]] is where you check that the interviews actually happened and that the person has had some training.

collocations: to carry out the periodic review
to verify that the interviews have been held
to hand a copy to the employee
note_fr: Notion sans équivalent étranger. L'enjeu à expliquer : dans les entreprises d'une certaine taille, l'employeur qui ne peut pas justifier des entretiens et d'une formation non obligatoire s'expose à devoir abonder le CPF du salarié. La périodicité a été modifiée par le législateur : vérifiez-la avant de citer un chiffre.

explain.written: The état des lieux récapitulatif is a written review which French law requires the employer to carry out at set intervals in order to verify that the employee has received the statutory career development interviews and has had access to training or progression.
explain.spoken: Every so many years there's a formal stocktake: you check, in writing, that the person has had their career interviews and at least some real training. If not, it can cost the company money.

def: A free and confidential advice service, provided in France by approved outside bodies, that helps any working person think through and plan a career move.

formal.ex: Employees shall be informed, at each career development interview, of their right to use the [[career guidance service (CEP)]].

everyday.ex: Before you do anything drastic, go and get some [[free career advice]]; it's confidential and it costs you nothing.
everyday.ex_us: Before you do anything drastic, go get some [[free career counseling]]; it's confidential and it costs you nothing.

collocations: to inform employees of their rights
note_fr: Dispositif public français sans équivalent exact : au Royaume-Uni, on penserait au « National Careers Service » ; aux États-Unis, à un « career counselor ». Orthographe : « adviser » ou « advisor », « counselling » (UK), « counseling » (US).

explain.written: The conseil en évolution professionnelle (CEP) is a free, confidential career guidance service, delivered by approved external bodies, which any working person in France may use to plan a career move or a training project.
explain.spoken: It's free, confidential career advice from an outside body. Any employee can use it, and the employer doesn't have to know.

def: A French scheme allowing an employee to take leave, with pay maintained in whole or in part, to follow a course leading to a qualification for a different occupation.

formal.uk: career transition leave (projet de transition professionnelle)
formal.us: career transition leave (projet de transition professionnelle)
formal.ex: An employee who meets the length-of-service conditions may apply for [[career transition leave (projet de transition professionnelle)]].

everyday.ex: She's applied for [[funded retraining leave]] to become a nurse, so we'll need cover for about a year.

collocations: to apply for career transition leave
to retrain for a new occupation
to return to one's post after the course
note_fr: Ce dispositif a remplacé le congé individuel de formation (CIF). Rien de comparable n'existe en droit britannique ou américain ; « sabbatical » ne convient pas, car il n'implique ni formation ni financement. Le contrat est suspendu, non rompu : le salarié retrouve son poste ou un poste équivalent.

explain.written: The projet de transition professionnelle is a scheme under French law which enables an employee to take leave in order to follow a qualifying course with a view to changing occupation, the contract being suspended and remuneration maintained in whole or in part by a dedicated funding body.
explain.spoken: It's a retraining leave. The employee goes off to train for a completely different job, a funding body covers most of the pay, and the contract is just suspended in the meantime.

def: One of the sector-based bodies, approved by the French State and run jointly by unions and employers, that fund work-study training and support smaller companies' training.

formal.ex: An application for funding shall be submitted to the relevant [[sector skills operator (OPCO)]] before the course begins.

everyday.ex: Our [[sector training fund]] will pay for the apprentice's course, so the cost to us is mostly her salary.

informal.ex: Have we heard back from the [[OPCO]]?

collocations: to apply to the OPCO for funding
note_fr: Aucun équivalent direct. Pour un Britannique, rapprochez-le des anciens « sector skills councils » en précisant le rôle de financeur ; pour un Américain, expliquez simplement « an industry training fund run jointly by unions and employers ». « Operator » seul évoque un standardiste ou un conducteur de machine : gardez le sigle et glosez.

explain.written: An OPCO (opérateur de compétences) is one of the sector-based bodies, approved by the State and jointly managed by employers' organisations and trade unions, which finance work-study contracts and assist smaller companies with their training needs.
explain.spoken: Each industry in France has a training fund run jointly by unions and employers. It pays for apprenticeships and helps smaller firms with training.

def: An extra amount paid into an employee's personal training account, by the employer or another funder, on top of the normal yearly credit.

formal.ex: The Company shall make an [[additional contribution]] to the personal training account of any employee who undertakes a course on the approved list.

everyday.ex: We've agreed to [[top up]] her training account so that she can do the full course.
everyday.ex_us: We've agreed to [[add to]] her training account so that she can do the full course.

note_fr: « Abundance » n'a aucun rapport. « Top-up » est britannique ; un Américain comprendra mieux « additional contribution » ou « employer match » (par analogie avec l'épargne retraite). L'abondement peut être volontaire, prévu par accord, ou imposé à titre de sanction (« corrective top-up ») lorsque l'employeur a manqué à ses obligations en matière d'entretiens.

explain.written: An abondement is an additional sum credited to an employee's personal training account (CPF) by the employer or another funder, whether voluntarily, under a collective agreement or as a penalty for failing to meet statutory obligations.
explain.spoken: It's a top-up to the employee's training account. The company can do it voluntarily to co-fund a course - and in some cases it has to, as a penalty.

def: A person's capacity to keep a job or find another; in France, the employer has a legal duty to help employees remain able to hold one.

formal.ex: The employer is under a [[duty to maintain employees' employability]], in particular in the light of changes in jobs, technology and organisation.

everyday.uk: to keep people's skills up to date
everyday.us: to keep people's skills up to date
everyday.ex: In France you have a legal duty to [[keep people's skills up to date]], whether or not they ask for training.

collocations: to adapt employees to their jobs
to be in breach of the duty to train
to keep pace with changes in the job
note_fr: Différence juridique majeure : l'employeur français doit assurer l'adaptation des salariés à leur poste et veiller au maintien de leur capacité à occuper un emploi ; un salarié resté des années sans formation peut obtenir réparation. Il n'existe pas d'obligation générale comparable en droit britannique ou américain.

explain.written: Under French law the employer must ensure that employees are adapted to their jobs and must see to it that they remain capable of holding a job, having regard in particular to changes in jobs, technology and organisation.
explain.spoken: In France the employer has a legal duty to keep people's skills current. If someone goes years without any training, the company can be held liable.

def: The process in which managers compare and adjust the ratings they propose so that standards are applied consistently across teams.

formal.ex: Proposed ratings are subject to [[calibration]] by a panel of managers before they are communicated to employees.

everyday.ex: My rating for her didn't survive the [[calibration meeting]], and now I have to explain why.
everyday.ex_us: My rating for her didn't survive the [[calibration session]], and now I have to explain why.

collocations: to move a rating up or down
to make the case for someone
note_fr: Le mot est le même, mais la pratique doit être expliquée avec soin en France : le salarié doit avoir été informé des méthodes d'évaluation, et les critères doivent être objectifs et pertinents. « To make the case for someone » = défendre le dossier de quelqu'un.

def: A system that requires managers to place fixed percentages of employees in each rating category.

formal.ex: The Company does not apply a [[forced distribution]] of ratings; the indicative ranges are for guidance only.

everyday.ex: Head office wants [[forced ranking]], and I've told them it would be very risky in France.

informal.ex: It's basically [[rank and yank]].

collocations: to rank employees against each other
note_fr: Pratique d'origine américaine. En France, les juges admettent des fourchettes indicatives mais condamnent les quotas imposés, qui conduisent à noter selon d'autres critères que les qualités professionnelles. « Rank and yank » est un terme familier et critique, à ne jamais écrire.

def: A systematic error of judgement made by the person rating performance, such as giving too much weight to recent events.

formal.ex: Appraisers receive training designed to reduce [[rater bias]], including recency and leniency effects.

everyday.ex: There's a lot of [[bias]] in the ratings; whoever shouts loudest gets the best score.

note_fr: « Bias » se prononce /ˈbaɪəs/ ; l'adjectif est « biased ». On est « biased towards » (UK) ou « toward » (US) ce qu'on favorise et « biased against » ce qu'on défavorise. « Recency bias » = surpondération des événements récents ; « leniency » = indulgence.

def: Feedback on a person collected, usually anonymously, from his or her manager, peers, direct reports and sometimes clients.

formal.ex: [[Multi-source feedback]] is used for development purposes only and has no bearing on remuneration.
formal.ex_us: [[Multi-rater feedback]] is used for development purposes only and has no bearing on compensation.

everyday.ex: We use [[360-degree feedback]] for everyone at director level and above.

informal.ex: I've got my [[360]] debrief on Monday and I'm dreading it.

note_fr: Se dit « three-sixty ». « Peers » = collègues de même niveau. En France, comme tout dispositif d'évaluation, le 360 suppose l'information préalable des salariés et la consultation du CSE ; l'anonymat des répondants doit être concilié avec le droit d'accès du salarié à ses données.

def: A meeting in which senior managers and HR discuss the performance and potential of employees and decide on development and succession.

formal.ex: The outcome of the [[talent review]] is confidential and is not, as such, communicated to the individuals concerned.

everyday.ex: Her name came up three times in the [[talent review]], which tells you something.

note_fr: « People review » est compris des anglophones, mais ce sont surtout les Français qui l'emploient ; le terme courant est « talent review ». Question sensible à anticiper : ce que l'on dit ou non au salarié de son classement, et son droit d'accès aux données qui le concernent.

def: A three-by-three table on which employees are placed according to their current performance and their potential.

formal.ex: Each employee in scope is positioned on the [[performance and potential matrix]] by the review committee.

everyday.ex: On the [[nine-box grid]] he's high performance, medium potential, and that feels right.
everyday.ex_us: On the [[nine-box]] he's high performance, medium potential, and that feels right.

collocations: to place someone on the grid
note_fr: « To plot X against Y » = placer X en fonction de Y sur un graphique. « A solid performer » est un compliment mesuré : quelqu'un de fiable, sans potentiel exceptionnel. « Top right » = la case des futurs dirigeants.

def: To translate the organisation's objectives into objectives for each division, team and individual in turn.

formal.ex: Corporate objectives are [[cascaded]] to business units in January and to individuals by the end of February.

everyday.ex: We need to [[break down]] the group target into something each team can actually own.

collocations: to cascade objectives down the organisation
to align individual and team objectives
note_fr: « To decline objectives » voudrait dire les refuser : contresens garanti. Dites « to cascade », « to break down » ou « to translate into ». « To own an objective » = en assumer la responsabilité.

def: The arrangement of jobs into levels according to their responsibility and difficulty, each level being linked to a pay range.

formal.ex: Positions are allocated to a grade within the Company's [[grading structure]] on the basis of objective criteria.
formal.ex_us: Positions are allocated to a grade within the Company's [[job classification system]] on the basis of objective criteria.

everyday.ex: She's moved up a [[grade]], so strictly speaking it is a promotion.
everyday.ex_us: She's moved up a [[level]], so strictly speaking it is a promotion.

collocations: to be at the top of one's grade
note_fr: « Classification » est rare dans l'usage britannique des RH, où l'on parle de « grading » ; les Américains disent « job leveling » ou « job classification ». En France, la classification découle de la convention collective : dites « the grading structure set by the collective agreement » et précisez que le coefficient détermine un salaire minimum.

def: A systematic method of comparing jobs, not the people who hold them, in order to decide their relative level.

formal.ex: A [[job evaluation]] shall be carried out whenever the content of a position changes substantially.

everyday.ex: We need to [[size the job]] properly before we advertise it.
everyday.ex_us: We need to [[level the job]] properly before we post it.

collocations: to benchmark a job against the market
note_fr: On évalue le poste, non son titulaire : la confusion avec « performance evaluation » est fréquente. « Job weighing » est un calque de « pesée ». Une pesée objective sert aussi à établir l'égalité de rémunération pour un travail de valeur égale (« work of equal value »).

def: A structure that lets specialists progress in grade and pay without having to become managers.

formal.ex: The [[dual career ladder]] enables technical experts to reach grades equivalent to those of senior managers.

everyday.ex: She doesn't want to manage people, so she's staying on the [[specialist track]].
everyday.ex_us: She doesn't want to manage people, so she's staying on the [[individual contributor track]].

informal.ex: He's happy on the [[IC track]].

note_fr: « Individual contributor » (IC) désigne, surtout aux États-Unis, un salarié sans équipe à encadrer, quel que soit son niveau. « Filière » se rend ici par « track » ou « ladder » ; « to climb the career ladder » = gravir les échelons.

def: A point in a career at which further promotion becomes unlikely.

formal.ex: The policy pays particular attention to employees who have reached a [[career plateau]].

everyday.ex: He [[plateaued]] about five years ago, and I think he knows it.

informal.ex: She feels [[stuck in a rut]].

note_fr: « To plateau » est aussi un verbe. L'accent tonique tombe sur la première syllabe en anglais britannique, sur la seconde en américain. « To stagnate » existe mais porte un jugement plus dur ; « stuck in a rut » = enlisé dans la routine.

def: The number and quality of people ready to step into key roles if they become vacant.

formal.ex: [[Succession cover]] for critical roles is reported to the board twice a year.
formal.ex_us: [[Succession coverage]] for critical roles is reported to the board twice a year.

everyday.ex: We've very little [[bench strength]] in finance; if she leaves, we're in trouble.
everyday.ex_us: We have very little [[bench strength]] in finance; if she leaves, we're in trouble.

note_fr: Métaphore sportive (le banc des remplaçants), d'origine américaine mais comprise partout. « Relève » ne se traduit pas par « relief » (soulagement, secours).

def: An employee thought likely to leave the organisation soon, or the likelihood itself.

formal.ex: The review identifies eleven employees in critical roles as a high [[retention risk]].

everyday.ex: I'd say he's a [[flight risk]]; he's been approached twice this year.

informal.ex: She's [[got itchy feet]].

collocations: to be at risk of leaving
to be approached by a headhunter
to have one foot out of the door
note_fr: « Flight risk » vient du vocabulaire judiciaire (risque de fuite d'un prévenu) : à l'oral entre professionnels des RH, jamais devant l'intéressé ni par écrit. « To be approached » = être sollicité par un recruteur.

def: A job whose vacancy would seriously harm the business and which is therefore a priority for succession planning.

formal.ex: A named successor shall be identified for each [[business-critical role]].

everyday.ex: It's a [[key role]], and at the moment only one person can do it.

note_fr: « Critical » signifie ici essentiel, pas critique au sens de défavorable. « A single point of failure » se dit d'une personne dont tout dépend. Évitez « key post », vieilli ; « post » pour un emploi est surtout britannique et administratif.

fr: mission de développement (hors zone de confort)
def: A project or task slightly beyond a person's current abilities, given in order to help him or her develop.

formal.ex: High-potential employees are offered at least one [[developmental assignment]] outside their own function.

everyday.ex: Leading the integration would be a real [[stretch assignment]] for her, which is exactly the point.

informal.uk: to throw someone in at the deep end
informal.us: to throw someone in at the deep end
informal.ex: They [[threw him in at the deep end]] and he coped brilliantly.

collocations: to take on a stretch assignment
to step outside one's comfort zone
to give someone exposure to senior management
note_fr: « Mission » en anglais évoque la raison d'être d'une entreprise ou une mission diplomatique ; pour un travail confié, dites « assignment » ou « project ». « Exposure » est positif ici : visibilité auprès de la direction.

fr: transfert des acquis de la formation
def: The extent to which people actually apply at work what they learnt in training.

formal.uk: transfer of learning to the workplace
formal.us: transfer of learning to the workplace
formal.ex: Line managers play a decisive part in the [[transfer of learning to the workplace]].
formal.ex_us: Managers play a decisive part in the [[transfer of learning to the workplace]].

everyday.ex: The course was fine; the problem is that nobody [[puts it into practice]] afterwards.

collocations: to apply what one has learnt
to follow up after a course
note_fr: « Acquis » se rend par « what has been learnt » ou « learning » (indénombrable), pas par « acquisitions ». « To embed » = ancrer durablement ; « to make it stick » en est la version orale.

fr: évaluation de la formation (à chaud / à froid)
def: The assessment of a course's quality and effects, immediately afterwards and again some months later.

formal.ex: A [[post-training evaluation]] is carried out at the end of each session and repeated three months later.

everyday.ex: Don't forget to fill in the [[feedback form]] before you leave.
everyday.ex_us: Don't forget to fill out the [[course evaluation]] before you leave.

informal.ex: The [[happy sheets]] were glowing, but has anything actually changed?
informal.ex_us: The [[smile sheets]] were glowing, but has anything actually changed?

collocations: to measure the impact of training
note_fr: « Hot » et « cold evaluation » ne sont pas idiomatiques : dites « immediate » ou « end-of-course evaluation » et « follow-up evaluation ». « Happy sheet » (UK) et « smile sheet » (US) sont des termes familiers et légèrement moqueurs pour le questionnaire de satisfaction.

def: Recording systematically which skills exist in an organisation, who has them and at what level.

formal.ex: The Company shall maintain an up-to-date [[skills inventory]] for each of its sites.

everyday.ex: Until we've [[mapped the skills]] we've got, we can't say what we're missing.
everyday.ex_us: Until we've [[mapped the skills]] we have, we can't say what we're missing.

collocations: to map skills against future needs
to carry out a skills audit
note_fr: « Cartography » ne s'emploie que pour les cartes géographiques. Dites « skills mapping », « skills audit » ou « skills inventory » ; le tableau croisant personnes et compétences est une « skills matrix ».
